concerns.canonical_paraphrase: The child says he still sees his friends at school but they do not ask him to things now — everybody went to the lake on Saturday and nobody said a word to him about it.
The child says he feels sick when he takes the morning medicine, and that the liquid one is hard to take and makes him gag every single time.
The child says his seven-year-old brother asks him whether it hurts and he tells him no, keeping the bad parts and the bad days from him, and that his brother has started asking their mother instead.
The parent says his friends message him and he leaves the messages sitting unopened, and that two of them came at the start and he would not come down.

The parent says the morning medicine undoes him on his steroid weeks — he gags on his liquid dexamethasone for a good twenty minutes before he will keep it down, and by then he is worn out and so is she.
The parent says he is careful with his brother to a fault: he will not say a word about a bad day where his brother can hear it, and he will do anything not to worry them.

The parent says that when it is something big, such as the bone marrow results, she wants both parents in the room to hear it together — twice somebody has told her alone in the hallway and she has carried it home to his father herself — and that their son is old enough to hear it when they do rather than learning it from whichever of them was told first.
The parent says that, small next to the rest of it, he missed the trip the whole grade went on in the spring and she has not found a way to make that up to him.
